title: Cashew nut shell-derived N-doped biochar–UiO-66-NH 2  MOF composite as a novel mesoporous adsorbent for the removal of toxic cationic dyes from water
content: With the increasing industrial use of synthetic dyes, their effective removal from industrial wastewater has become an important aspect of water treatment. Bio-waste-derived adsorbents have attracted considerable attention as sustainable and cost-effective materials for dye remediation. In this study, cashew nut shell-derived biochar (BC) was activated using NH4OH and subsequently integrated with amino-functionalized UiO-66-NH2 through an in situ solvothermal process to fabricate a UiO-66-NH2/BC composite. The synthesized material was systematically characterized using XRD, FTIR SEM–EDS, TEM, XPS, zeta potential analysis and BET surface area measurements to investigate its structural, morphological, surface chemical and textural properties. The composite exhibited a mesoporous structure with a specific surface area of 153.21 m2 g−1, a total pore volume of 0.1756 cm3 g−1 and an average pore diameter of 4.59 nm. Its adsorption performance was evaluated using two cationic dyes, crystal violet (CV) and methylene blue (MB), under different experimental conditions. Maximum removal efficiencies of approximately 95.8% for CV and 94.8% for MB were achieved under optimized conditions (adsorbent dosage = 0.025 g, contact time = 100 min and pH = 7). The adsorption kinetic data were well described by the pseudo-second-order model, while the equilibrium data exhibited a better fit to the Langmuir isotherm model, with maximum adsorption capacities of 210 mg g−1 for CV and 202.69 mg g−1 for MB. The mechanism of the reaction was evaluated using spectral analysis, and it was found that the primary electrostatic attraction of the functional groups, reinforced by π–π stacking, is responsible for the adsorption process. The composite demonstrated good reusability over five consecutive adsorption–desorption cycles, demonstrating that it is a sustainable, mechanistically well-characterized and reusable adsorbent for cationic dye-contaminated wastewater treatment.
